Introduction

Thank you for trying this module. Tianze's Otari Extras is a collection of maps and content set in the town of Otari, which is the setting for Pathfinder scenarios including Menace Under Otari (the Beginner Box adventure), Abomination Vaults Adventure Path and Troubles in Otari. 

Maps were created with DungeonDraft using assets from Forgotten Adventures.

Portraits and vignettes were created using Bing Image Creator.

Tianze's Otari Extras is a collection of maps and content for the Otari area. It includes Crook's Nook and the Underbridge, Crow's Casks, Otari Market, the ruins of the Thirsty Alpaca and the Fish Camp Base.

Acrobats perform feats of agility, balance, and strength. The acrobat is a 5th-level challenge for contests of acrobatics and the like.

Performances can serve as entertainment, expressions of beauty, or part of a shared culture.

When the acrobat rolls a success on an Acrobatics check, they get a critical success instead.

They aren't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} when attempting to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance} and can attempt an Acrobatics check instead of a Reflex save to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge}.
The acrobat treats all falls as 50 feet shorter.

Trigger The acrobat is targeted with a melee or ranged attack by an attacker they can see

Effect The acrobat gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.
The acrobat swings on a rope or trapeze, moving up to double their Speed. At any point during the swing, they can make a melee Strike.

By setting ambushes and traps in concealing countryside, such as forests and mountains, bandits waylay travelers and plunder their valuables before disappearing back to their wilderness hideouts. Many bandits seek only to steal and release their victims alive, though a few prefer to leave no witnesses.

Some criminals are the desperate who have no option but to break the law to survive, while others choose a life of crime for thrills, forming gangs or underworld guilds that specialize in certain illegal ventures.
When the bandit rolls initiative using Deception or Stealth, they can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} one creature as a free action.
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} creatures are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the bandit.
The bandit ignores the effects of non-magical difficult terrain in forests.

Magical Sundries

Bethela is seventeen years old, and recently returned from magical studies in Absalom.

Even though her family lives in town, she is accustomed to her independence and now rents a room from Alymora Inkleholtz.

In the mornings, she sells magical items from Wrin's Wonders and Odd Stories, and in the afternoons she tutors the Inlkeholtz children.

She is saving money to return to Absalom and open a magic item stall of her own.

Activate @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.KjoCEEmPGTeFE4hh]{Treat Poison}

This dried herb is known for its ability to draw toxins from the body, albeit violently. You can administer the suspension orally, Activating the item as part of the same activity you use to Treat Poison. If you succeed at your Medicine check to Treat Poison against an ingested poison, you can reduce the stage of the toxin by one stage, though this can't reduce the stage below stage 1 or cure the poison entirely. If you do, the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} as its body purges the toxin. An artevil suspension doesn't work unless the poison was administered through ingestion; for instance, if a poison can be administered through either ingestion or injury and was administered through injury, the suspension won't work.

The boggard swampseer has been gifted with magic through their worship of the demon lord Gogunta, and they use their power to rule a boggard village, keeping the rest of the village in line and planning raids on nearby communities.

Boggards are aggressive humanoid amphibians who thrive in swamps, marshes, and even some rain forests. Boggards hatch from eggs into tadpoles, fiercely competing for food and even consuming their siblings in that struggle. Over 3 years, the surviving boggards develop arms, legs, and lungs while learning the rudiments of hunting, crafts, and warfare—everything needed to survive in their might-makes-right society. At the top of most boggard hierarchies lords a hulking swampseer imbued with sinister divine magic.
Variant Boggard Swampseer

The swampseer utters a powerful croak that deals @Damage[4d6[sonic]] damage to any non-boggard within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15] (@Check[type:fortitude|dc:19|basic:true] save); any creature with the frightened condition takes additional sonic damage equal to twice the value of its frightened condition.

The boggard can't use Destructive Croak again for [[/br 1d4 #Recharge use Destructive Croak]]{1d4 rounds}.

Trigger The boggard swampseer or one of their allies within 60 feet attempts a saving throw against an auditory or sonic effect

Effect The swampseer releases a croak that drowns out other sounds. They roll a @Check[type:performance] check. They and boggard allies in the area can use the higher result between the swampseer's Performance check and their saves to resolve the effects against the auditory or sonic effect.
A boggard shoreseer ignores difficult terrain caused by sandy terrain features.

The boggard swampseer unleashes a terrifying croak. Any non-boggard within @Template[type:emanation|distance:30]{30 feet} becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} unless they succeed at a @Check[type:will|dc:19] save; those who critically succeed are temporarily immune for 1 minute.

If the boggard swampseer hits a creature with their tongue, that creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the boggard. Unlike with a normal Grab, the creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, but it can't move beyond the reach of the boggard's tongue. A creature can sever the tongue by hitting AC 15 and dealing at least 4 slashing damage. Though this doesn't deal any damage to the boggard, it prevents them from using their tongue Strike until they regrow their tongue, which takes a week.

Boggard Armor is made from the shells of turtules. The armor consists of a breastplate made from the shells of small turtles sewn onto a leather jerkin, with pauldrons, braciers and greaves made from a single larger shell.

It is equivalent to studded leather armor, but is worth more due to its unusual materials and construction.

This necklace has 31 sharks' teeth arranged with the longest in the center and the shortest at the ends. They are pierced at the thick end and arranged on a strand of sinew. It is about 20 inches long.

Some criminals are the desperate who have no option but to break the law to survive, while others choose a life of crime for thrills, forming gangs or underworld guilds that specialize in certain illegal ventures.

Clodia's Clothery

Clodia is a clothier with a perpetual squint from a lifetime of up-close work. Her thick and expensive glasses no longer really help.

She carries clothing in a variety of sizes for small and medium creatures, and can make alternations to fit.

Clodia is a true artist, even if she has humble means. She loves nothing more to see someone beautifully clothed in her work.

Crook's Nook

Crooks Nook is a popular tavern offering brews, meals and fishing.

Patrons can either bring their own fishing rods, or use one of the rods on the rack between the fireplaces.

Yinyasmera will buy fresh fish, but only one bulk at a time, assuming each fish weighs one light. She will pay one silver piece per bulk.

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

To Cast a Spell from a scroll, the spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack roll and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical material components and costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when Casting a Spell from a scroll. You must replace any required material component for that spell with a somatic component. If the spell requires a focus, you must have that focus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WBmvzNDfpwka3qT4]{Light}

In an effort to spread the knowledge of magic as widely as possible, worshippers of Nethys discovered a way to bind cantrips into cards accessible even to non-spellcasters. The deck contains thick parchment cards, each roughly half the size of a playing card. In precise, no-nonsense script, each card simply states the name of its cantrip, color-coded based on its school.

This pack contains 5 cards of a single common cantrip.

Activate 1 or more (envision, Interact)

Effect You envision your desired cantrip, causing its card to rise to the top of the deck, and draw the card. The deck casts that cantrip as a 1st-level spell, with a DC of 15 and a spell attack modifier of +5. The card crumbles into dust as the cantrip takes effect. The activation takes the same number of actions as the cantrip you chose takes to cast.

Dawnflower Library

The Library sells items and weapons, but will only purchase items that would fit in with their usual stock.

They absolutely will not purchase any item that they perceive as evil. They will urge the heroes to leave any such items with them for disposal.

They will cast spells, such as for disease curing and curse removals, for the same cost it would be to make a scroll for the same spell.

If, as part of a curse removal, a hero needs to be rid of a cursed item, they accept such items for disposal free of charge, but may ask for a quest to facilitate any difficult-to-destroy items.

Also Crisp and Fresh

This stall is owned by Jala Highstepper.

Dori was sent by her father, the mayor, to apprentice with Jala Highstepper. She has been glum at the prospect, but reluctantly obeys.
This is a single serving common fruit that is in-season for the area.

Brelda's Bakery

When Brelda's son disappeard, her good friend and fellow dwarven matron Drarda offered to run her market stall while Brelda runs her son's inn.

Drarda is the widow of Trusk Hanely, the former Captain of the Guard. She fetches Brelda's baked goods every morning and is usually sold out in time for lunch. She is quite happy running the market stall, as helping Brelda has helped her reconcile herself with the loss of her husband.

The drunken brawler can still @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} while in a drunken rage. This armor is simply a layer of heavy, quilted cloth, but it is sometimes used because it's so inexpensive. Padded armor is easier to damage and destroy than other types of armor. Heavy armor comes with a padded armor undercoat included in its Price, though it loses the comfort trait when worn under heavy armor. You can wear just that padded armor or undercoat to sleep in, if your heavy armor is destroyed, or when otherwise not wearing the full heavy armor. This allows you to keep the armor invested and benefit from the power of any runes on the associated heavy armor, but no one else can wear your heavy armor without the padded undercoat.
